title: If sentences
description: Say what happens, will happen or would happen if something is true.

guide.summary: Si sentences link a condition to its result. Decide first whether the condition is real or imagined: that single choice fixes the tense in both clauses.

sections.title: Real or imagined?
sections.text: The clause with si gives the condition, the other clause gives the result. Everything depends on whether the condition could really happen or is only imagined.
steps: Find the two clauses: the one with si is the condition.
Decide: could it really happen, or are you only imagining it?
Take that line of the table and give each clause its tense.

examples.fr: Si tu viens ce soir, on ira au cinéma.
examples.en: If you come tonight, we’ll go to the cinema.

examples.fr: Si j’avais le temps, je voyagerais plus souvent.
examples.en: If I had the time, I would travel more often.

watch: The two tenses come as a pair: an imparfait after si never goes with a futur result, and a présent after si never goes with a conditionnel result.
French and English agree here: after if English also says “if you come”, not “if you will come”.

sections.title: Real condition: si + présent
sections.text: When the condition can really happen, the verb after si is in the présent. Only the result clause changes, depending on what you are doing with it.

rows: a habit or a general truth
Si on fait du sport, on dort mieux.
Si tu viens, on ira au cinéma.
advice or an order, with no subject

steps: Put the verb after si in the présent, with the ending of its own subject.
Ask what the result does: state a rule, announce the future, or tell someone what to do.
Take that line: présent, futur simple, or impératif with the subject pronoun dropped.

examples.fr: Si tu chauffes la glace, elle fond.
examples.en: If you heat ice, it melts.

examples.fr: Si elle a le temps, elle te téléphonera demain.
examples.en: If she has time, she will phone you tomorrow.

examples.fr: Si tu as froid, mets un pull.
examples.en: If you are cold, put a jumper on.

watch: The impératif is the présent form with the pronoun dropped: vous prenez → prenez.
In the tu impératif, -er verbs lose the final s (mange, regarde) but other verbs keep it (prends, mets).
A futur is welcome in the result clause; after si it never is.

sections.title: Imagined condition: si + imparfait, result in the conditionnel
sections.text: The imparfait is built on the nous form of the présent (nous avons → av-). The conditionnel takes the futur stem, usually the whole infinitive, plus the imparfait endings.
steps: Put the verb after si in the imparfait.
Build the result on the futur stem with the same endings: -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient.
Match each ending to the subject of its own clause.

examples.fr: Si nous étions riches, nous achèterions une maison à la mer.
examples.en: If we were rich, we would buy a house by the sea.

examples.fr: Si elle parlait espagnol, elle travaillerait à Madrid.
examples.en: If she spoke Spanish, she would work in Madrid.

watch: The stems are the futur ones: être → ser-, avoir → aur-, aller → ir-, pouvoir → pourr-, venir → viendr-.
-ais, -ait and -aient all sound the same, so choose the ending from the subject, not from the sound.
The imparfait after si is not a past: si j’avais le temps means “if I had the time” now or in general.

sections.title: What can never follow si
sections.text: Si takes no futur and no conditionnel, however future or imaginary the meaning is. Those two forms belong in the result clause.

rows: move it to the result clause
move it to the result clause

steps: Look at the verb immediately after si.
Endings in -ra, -rai, -rons mark a futur; -rais, -rait, -raient mark a conditionnel. Either one is in the wrong clause.
Swap it for the présent when the result is a futur or an order, for the imparfait when the result is a conditionnel.
Leave the result clause alone: it is allowed to keep its futur or conditionnel.

examples.fr: S’il fait beau demain, nous irons à la plage.
examples.en: If the weather is nice tomorrow, we’ll go to the beach.

examples.fr: Si elle était là, elle nous aiderait.
examples.en: If she were here, she would help us.

watch: Demain, ce soir and l’année prochaine change the meaning, never the tense after si.
Si j’aurais and si je serais are the classic slips: after si those verbs go into the imparfait.

sections.title: Si, s’il, s’ils

rows: S’ils viennent, on fera un gâteau.
Si elle vient, je serai content.
Si on part tôt, on arrivera à midi.

steps: Look at the word standing right after si.
Only il and ils make si drop its i, with an apostrophe and no space.
Before anything else, elle and elles included, si stays whole.

examples.fr: S’ils ont faim, ils mangeront une pizza.
examples.en: If they are hungry, they will eat a pizza.

examples.fr: Si elle arrive tôt, elle nous attendra.
examples.en: If she arrives early, she will wait for us.

watch: Si il and si ils are always wrong; s’elle and s’on do not exist.
Même si obeys the same rule: même s’il fait froid.

sections.title: Which clause comes first?
sections.text: Either clause can open the sentence. The tenses stay with their own clause; only the punctuation changes.

rows: Si j’avais le temps, je voyagerais.
Je voyagerais si j’avais le temps.

steps: Identify the condition and the result.
Move the whole clause, verb included, and keep its tense exactly as it was.
Write a comma only when the si clause comes first.

examples.fr: Appelle-moi si tu as besoin d’aide.
examples.en: Call me if you need help.

examples.fr: Je t’aiderai si tu me le demandes.
examples.en: I’ll help you if you ask me to.

watch: A si clause at the end still refuses the futur and the conditionnel.

sections.title: Même si (even if)
sections.text: Même si means “even if”: the result happens anyway. Its tenses work exactly like si’s.

rows: Même si elle avait le temps, elle ne viendrait pas.

steps: Read même si as si: the tense rules are identical.
Choose présent with a présent, futur or impératif result, or imparfait with a conditionnel result.
Contract before il and ils: même s’il, même s’ils.

examples.fr: Je finirai ce travail même si je suis fatigué.
examples.en: I’ll finish this work even if I’m tired.

examples.fr: Il ira au travail même s’il est malade.
examples.en: He will go to work even if he is sick.

watch: Neither a futur nor a conditionnel may stand straight after même si.

steps: Check the result: a habit or a general truth stays in the présent.
Put the verb after si in the présent too, with the ending of its subject.
Keep both clauses in the présent: no futur and no conditionnel anywhere.
Check that the condition is real: the verb after si is a présent.
Build the result on the futur stem plus -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont.
Leave the si clause in the présent, even when the sentence talks about demain.
Spot the result with no subject pronoun: it is an order or a piece of advice.
Take the présent form for tu or vous and drop the pronoun.
Remember the tu form of -er verbs loses its final s; the verb after si stays in the présent.
Check the pair: one clause is an imparfait, the other a conditionnel.
After si, use the imparfait: présent nous stem plus -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient.
In the result, use the futur stem with those same endings.
Match each ending to the subject of its own clause.
Find the verb standing directly after si.
An ending in -ra/-rai/-rons (futur) or -rais/-rait/-raient (conditionnel) means it must change.
Use the présent when the result is a futur or an order, the imparfait when the result is a conditionnel.
Change nothing in the result clause: it may keep its futur or conditionnel.
Look at the word straight after si.
Before il or ils, join them with an apostrophe and no space.
Before anything else, elle and elles included, leave si whole.
Decide which clause opens the sentence.
Move it whole: reordering never changes a tense.
Add a comma only if the si clause comes first.
Treat même si exactly like si when choosing the tenses.
Pick présent with a présent, futur or impératif result, or imparfait with a conditionnel result.
Elide to même s’il / même s’ils before il and ils.

exercises.source: Si on ____ du sport, on dort mieux.
answers: fait
exercises.hint: The result, on dort, is in the présent. What tense goes after si in a real condition?
exercises.feedback: After si, French never uses the futur or the conditionnel.
exercises.explanation: A real condition takes si + présent: si on fait du sport, on dort mieux. It states a general truth.

answers: fera
mistakes.why: Fera is the futur simple of faire. French never puts a futur after si, however future the meaning is.

answers: ferait
mistakes.why: Ferait is a conditionnel, the mood for the result of an imagined condition. Here the result on dort is a plain présent, and nothing in that mood may follow si.

exercises.instruction: Write chauffer in the right form.
exercises.source: Si tu ____ (chauffer) la glace, elle fond.
answers: chauffes
exercises.hint: Elle fond is a general truth in the présent. The si clause matches it.
exercises.feedback: Use the présent after si, with the tu ending.
exercises.explanation: Si + présent, result in the présent: si tu chauffes la glace, elle fond.

answers: chaufferas
mistakes.why: That is the futur simple. Elle fond states what always happens, and after si the verb stays in the présent anyway.

answers: chaufferais
mistakes.why: That is the conditionnel, which can never follow si.

answers: chauffe
mistakes.why: That is the il/elle form. The subject here is tu, which takes its own ending in the présent.

answers: chauffais
mistakes.why: That is the imparfait. An imparfait after si sets up an imagined condition and calls for a conditionnel result, but elle fond is a simple fact.

exercises.source: If I’m tired, I go to bed early.
answers: Si je suis fatigué, je me couche tôt.
Si je suis fatiguée, je me couche tôt.
Je me couche tôt si je suis fatigué.
Je me couche tôt si je suis fatiguée.
Si je suis fatigué, je vais au lit tôt.
Si je suis fatiguée, je vais au lit tôt.
Je vais au lit tôt si je suis fatigué.
Je vais au lit tôt si je suis fatiguée.
spellingAnswers: Si je suis fatigué je me couche tôt.
Si je suis fatiguée je me couche tôt.
exercises.hint: This is a habit: both verbs stay in the présent. Go to bed is the reflexive verb se coucher.
exercises.feedback: Keep both verbs in the présent: a habit needs no futur or conditionnel.
exercises.explanation: A habit takes si + présent and a result in the présent: si je suis fatigué, je me couche tôt.

answers: Si je serai fatigué, je me couche tôt.
Si je serai fatiguée, je me couche tôt.
mistakes.why: Serai is a futur simple, and a futur is never allowed after si.

answers: Si je suis fatigué, je me coucherai tôt.
Si je suis fatiguée, je me coucherai tôt.
mistakes.why: This announces one future evening. The English sentence describes a habit, so the result stays in the présent.

answers: Si je suis fatigué, je couche tôt.
Si je suis fatiguée, je couche tôt.
mistakes.why: Coucher on its own means to put someone else to bed. Going to bed yourself needs the reflexive pronoun in front of the verb.

answers: Si je serais fatigué, je me coucherais tôt.
Si je serais fatiguée, je me coucherais tôt.
mistakes.why: Two conditionnels: si takes none, and nothing here is imagined — it is what you always do.

exercises.instruction: Join the two sentences into one: put si before the first sentence and keep both verbs in the présent.
exercises.source: Tu mélanges le bleu et le jaune. Tu obtiens du vert.
answers: Si tu mélanges le bleu et le jaune, tu obtiens du vert.
spellingAnswers: Si tu mélanges le bleu et le jaune tu obtiens du vert.
exercises.hint: The first sentence is the condition. Si goes in front of it, then a comma, then the result.
exercises.feedback: Start with Si tu mélanges… and separate the two clauses with a comma.
exercises.explanation: Si + présent, then the result in the présent: a general truth about colours.

answers: Si tu mélanges le bleu et le jaune, tu obtiendras du vert.
mistakes.why: The result was moved to the futur. Mixing those colours always gives the same thing, and the instruction was to keep both verbs as they are.

answers: Si tu mélangeais le bleu et le jaune, tu obtiendrais du vert.
mistakes.why: Imparfait plus conditionnel makes the whole thing imagined. This is a general truth about colours, so the condition is real.

answers: Si tu mélanges le bleu et le jaune. Tu obtiens du vert.
mistakes.why: Si was added but the two sentences stayed apart. A condition and its result form one sentence, joined by a comma.

answers: Tu mélanges le bleu et le jaune si tu obtiens du vert.
mistakes.why: This reverses the logic: it makes the green the condition. Si goes in front of the mixing, which is what causes the result.

exercises.source: If you eat too much, you get a stomach ache.
answers: Si on mange trop, on a mal au ventre.
exercises.hint: A general truth: si + présent, then the result in the présent.
exercises.feedback: One of the verb tiles is a futur, which cannot follow si.
exercises.explanation: Si on mange trop uses the présent after si; on a mal au ventre states the general result.

answers: Si on mangera trop, on a mal au ventre.
mistakes.why: Mangera is a futur, and a futur can never sit after si.

answers: Si on mange trop, on mangera mal au ventre.
mistakes.why: The futur tile was used in the result, where it makes no sense: having an ache uses avoir, not manger.

exercises.source: Si tu viens ce soir, on ____ au cinéma.
answers: ira
exercises.hint: Tu viens is in the présent: the condition is real. What tense gives a future result?
exercises.feedback: A présent after si pairs with a futur (or présent, or impératif), not with a conditionnel or an imparfait.
exercises.explanation: Si + présent, result in the futur simple: si tu viens ce soir, on ira au cinéma.

answers: irait
mistakes.why: Irait is a conditionnel. It answers an imparfait after si, but tu viens is a présent, so the condition is real.

answers: allait
mistakes.why: Allait is the imparfait of aller, a past or imagined form. A real condition in the présent looks forward instead.

exercises.instruction: Write téléphoner in the futur simple.
exercises.source: Si elle a le temps, elle te ____ (téléphoner) demain.
answers: téléphonera
exercises.hint: The condition is real (si + présent). The result is in the future.
exercises.feedback: Use the futur simple: infinitive + the elle ending.
exercises.explanation: Si elle a le temps (présent), elle te téléphonera (futur simple).

answers: téléphone
mistakes.why: That is the présent, which would turn the sentence into a habit. Demain points to one future event.

answers: téléphonerait
mistakes.why: That is the conditionnel. It goes with an imparfait after si, but elle a le temps is a présent.

answers: téléphonerai
mistakes.why: That is the je form of the futur. The person phoning here is elle.

answers: téléphoneras
mistakes.why: That is the tu form. The subject of the result clause is elle, not the person being phoned.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French, using the futur simple. You can say we with on or nous.
exercises.source: If you (to a friend) come, we will go to the cinema.
answers: Si tu viens, on ira au cinéma.
Si tu viens, nous irons au cinéma.
On ira au cinéma si tu viens.
Nous irons au cinéma si tu viens.
spellingAnswers: Si tu viens on ira au cinéma.
Si tu viens nous irons au cinéma.
exercises.hint: English uses the present after if, and so does French. Will go becomes a futur simple.
exercises.feedback: Do not put a futur after si: the English present come stays a présent.
exercises.explanation: Si + présent (tu viens), result in the futur simple (on ira / nous irons).

alternatives.answer: Si tu viens, on va aller au cinéma.
alternatives.message: Correct French, but this exercise practises the futur simple after a si clause in the présent: on ira.

alternatives.answer: Si tu viens, nous allons aller au cinéma.
alternatives.message: Correct French, but this exercise practises the futur simple after a si clause in the présent: nous irons.

answers: Si tu viendras, on ira au cinéma.
Si tu viendras, nous irons au cinéma.
mistakes.why: Viendras is a futur. The English come is a present after if, and French keeps the présent there too.

answers: Si tu viens, on irait au cinéma.
Si tu viens, nous irions au cinéma.
mistakes.why: A conditionnel result needs an imparfait after si. Tu viens is a présent, so the plan is real, not imagined.

answers: Si tu viens, on va au cinéma.
Si tu viens, nous allons au cinéma.
mistakes.why: That présent describes a habit, not a plan. The exercise asks for the futur simple of aller.

exercises.instruction: Put the result clause in the futur simple.
exercises.source: Si tu travailles bien, tu réussis ton examen.
answers: Si tu travailles bien, tu réussiras ton examen.
spellingAnswers: Si tu travailles bien tu réussiras ton examen.
exercises.hint: Only the second verb changes. The verb after si stays in the présent.
exercises.feedback: Leave tu travailles as it is and change réussis.
exercises.explanation: Si + présent, result in the futur simple: tu réussiras.

answers: Si tu travailles bien, tu réussis ton examen.
mistakes.why: Nothing was changed: the result is still a présent, which states a general truth rather than a future outcome.

answers: Si tu travailleras bien, tu réussiras ton examen.
mistakes.why: The verb after si was changed too, and into a futur, which that position never allows.

answers: Si tu travailles bien, tu réussirais ton examen.
mistakes.why: Réussirais is a conditionnel, which needs an imparfait after si. The condition here stays real.

exercises.source: aller · on · futur simple
answers: ira
on ira
exercises.hint: Aller has an irregular futur stem: ir-.
exercises.feedback: The futur of aller is built on ir-, plus the on ending.
exercises.explanation: On ira, as in si tu viens, on ira au cinéma.

answers: va
on va
mistakes.why: That is the présent of aller. The question asks for the futur simple, which is built on a different stem.

answers: allera
on allera
mistakes.why: Aller does not build its futur on the infinitive: it uses a short irregular stem.

answers: irait
on irait
mistakes.why: That is the conditionnel présent. It shares the futur stem but takes the imparfait endings.

answers: irons
nous irons
mistakes.why: That is the nous form. On always takes the same ending as il and elle.

exercises.source: S’il pleut, ____ un parapluie.
answers: prends
exercises.hint: There is no subject in the result clause: it is an instruction.
exercises.feedback: An instruction with no subject uses the impératif.
exercises.explanation: Si + présent can be followed by an impératif: s’il pleut, prends un parapluie.

answers: prendrais
mistakes.why: Prendrais is a conditionnel and needs a subject (je or tu). The result clause here has no subject: it gives advice.

answers: prenais
mistakes.why: Prenais is the imparfait, a past or imagined form, and it also needs a subject. Advice after a real condition is given as an order.

exercises.source: Si tu as froid, ____ (mettre) un pull.
answers: mets
exercises.hint: Give advice to a friend with no subject pronoun.
exercises.feedback: The tu impératif of mettre is the tu présent form without tu.
exercises.explanation: Si + présent, then an impératif: si tu as froid, mets un pull.

answers: met
mistakes.why: That is the il/elle form of the présent. An order to a friend is built on the tu form, which ends differently.

answers: mettes
mistakes.why: That is a subjonctif form. An order for tu is simply the présent tu form with the pronoun dropped.

answers: mettre
mistakes.why: That is the infinitive. An instruction needs a conjugated form.

answers: tu mets
mistakes.why: The pronoun has to go: an impératif names nobody, it just gives the order.

answers: mettez
mistakes.why: That is the vous form. Si tu as froid speaks to one friend.

exercises.source: If you (to a friend) are hungry, eat an apple.
answers: Si tu as faim, mange une pomme.
Mange une pomme si tu as faim.
spellingAnswers: Si tu as faim mange une pomme.
exercises.hint: Be hungry is avoir faim. Eat is an instruction to one friend.
exercises.feedback: The -er impératif for tu has no final s: mange.
exercises.explanation: Si + présent (tu as faim), result in the impératif (mange).

answers: Si tu as faim, manges une pomme.
Manges une pomme si tu as faim.
mistakes.why: The tu order of an -er verb drops the final s of the présent form.

answers: Si tu es faim, mange une pomme.
mistakes.why: Être does not work here: French says to have hunger, so the si clause needs avoir.

answers: Si tu as faim, tu manges une pomme.
mistakes.why: With a subject pronoun this becomes a statement about a habit, not the instruction the English eat gives.

answers: Si tu auras faim, mange une pomme.
mistakes.why: Auras is a futur, and a futur can never follow si.

exercises.source: prendre · vous · impératif
answers: prenez
exercises.hint: The vous impératif is the vous présent form without vous.
exercises.feedback: Take the present form vous …ez and drop the pronoun.
exercises.explanation: Prenez, as in si vous êtes pressés, prenez un taxi.

answers: vous prenez
mistakes.why: Keeping the pronoun makes it an ordinary statement in the présent. An order drops it.

answers: prends
mistakes.why: That is the order for tu, one friend. The question asks for the form used with vous.

answers: prendez
mistakes.why: Prendre is not an -er verb: it loses the d of its stem in the plural of the présent.

answers: prenez-vous
mistakes.why: That is the inverted question form. An order is not a question and adds no pronoun.

exercises.source: If you (plural) are lost, call me.
answers: Si vous êtes perdus, appelez-moi.
exercises.hint: The result is an instruction. Which verb form after si goes with an impératif?
exercises.feedback: An imparfait after si belongs with a conditionnel, not an impératif.
exercises.explanation: Si + présent (vous êtes), result in the impératif (appelez-moi).

answers: Si vous étiez perdus, appelez-moi.
mistakes.why: Étiez is an imparfait: it makes the condition imagined and calls for a conditionnel result, not an order. Being lost is a real possibility, so the si clause stays in the présent.

exercises.source: Si j’avais le temps, je ____ plus souvent.
answers: voyagerais
exercises.hint: J’avais is an imparfait after si. Which mood gives the imagined result?
exercises.feedback: An imparfait after si needs the conditionnel présent, with the je ending.
exercises.explanation: Si + imparfait, result in the conditionnel présent: je voyagerais.

answers: voyagerai
mistakes.why: That is the futur simple. A futur result answers a condition in the présent, but j’avais is an imparfait.

answers: voyageais
mistakes.why: That is the imparfait. The imparfait belongs after si; the result of an imagined condition takes the other mood.

answers: voyagerait
mistakes.why: That is the il/elle ending. The subject of the result clause is je.

exercises.source: Si nous ____ riches, nous achèterions une maison à la mer.
answers: étions
exercises.hint: Nous achèterions is a conditionnel. What tense goes after si then?
exercises.feedback: The conditionnel never goes after si; it belongs in the result.
exercises.explanation: Si + imparfait (étions), result in the conditionnel (achèterions).

answers: serions
mistakes.why: Serions is the conditionnel of être, and a conditionnel never follows si: one already stands in the result, achèterions.

answers: sommes
mistakes.why: Sommes is the présent, which makes the condition real. A real condition does not pair with a conditionnel result.

answers: serons
mistakes.why: Serons is the futur simple, and a futur is never allowed after si.

exercises.instruction: Write travailler in the conditionnel présent.
exercises.source: Si elle parlait espagnol, elle ____ (travailler) à Madrid.
answers: travaillerait
exercises.hint: Parlait is an imparfait after si, so the result is imagined.
exercises.feedback: Use the infinitive plus the imparfait ending for elle.
exercises.explanation: Si + imparfait, result in the conditionnel présent: elle travaillerait.

answers: travaillait
mistakes.why: That is the imparfait, the form that belongs after si. The result of an imagined condition takes the other mood.

answers: travaillera
mistakes.why: That is the futur simple. A futur result goes with a présent after si, but parlait is an imparfait.

answers: travaillerai
mistakes.why: That mixes two things up: -ai is the je ending of the futur, and the subject here is elle.

answers: travaillerais
mistakes.why: That is the je or tu ending. The subject elle takes the third-person ending.

exercises.source: Si tu ____ (avoir) une voiture, tu viendrais nous voir.
answers: avais
exercises.hint: Tu viendrais is a conditionnel: the condition is imagined.
exercises.feedback: An imagined condition uses the imparfait after si.
exercises.explanation: Si + imparfait (tu avais), result in the conditionnel (tu viendrais).

answers: aurais
mistakes.why: Aurais is a conditionnel, and the conditionnel already stands in the result, tu viendrais. After si the verb takes the other tense.

answers: avait
mistakes.why: That is the il/elle form. The subject here is tu, which has its own ending.

answers: as
mistakes.why: As is the présent, which makes the condition real. Tu viendrais is a conditionnel, so the condition is imagined.

answers: auras
mistakes.why: Auras is a futur, which can never follow si.

exercises.source: If I were rich, I would buy a house.
answers: Si j’étais riche, j’achèterais une maison.
J’achèterais une maison si j’étais riche.
Si j’étais riche, je m’achèterais une maison.
Je m’achèterais une maison si j’étais riche.
